question: Is the line of scrimmage derived in Phase 3 wrong, in yards?
key_statistic: LOS time bound / |median gap| (bound 0.3 yd at 2.053 yd/s)
note: the recorded line is validated against the offensive line's own body positions and the share of players on the expected side; the formula is right in all four side/direction branches and the sign of travel is correct on 99.9% of defensive reps. An LOS error is bounded by the snapper's body geometry and cannot reach the median gap.

question: Is play_direction, the along-direction projection or the depth sign wrong?
key_statistic: share of defensive reps moving against the offence
note: a mirrored axis makes the depth non-positive for essentially every rep (the sample has 5.6% non-positive, all near zero, not 100%), and the observed motion direction agrees with the play direction on 99.9% of reps. See los_validation.csv.

question: Which crossing definition matches the label?
key_statistic: best plane offset (yd) and RMSE (s); within-play slope of implied distance on depth
note: a plane at depth + 0.75 yd removes the median gap and cuts RMSE from 0.4552 s to 0.1674 s. The paired within-play slope is 0.9893 +/- 0.1135 (n=44 reps, 22 plays): 1 = a plane, 0 = a fixed first-step distance. A fitted clock offset gives RMSE 0.2051 s and cannot fit the speed-dependent gap. WHICH body point is not identifiable: no bounding box and no ball are in the released files, so the offset is a structurally supported FIT, not a verified definition.

question: Is onset detection absorbing part of the difference?
note: cross_time_s is computed from the snap; the onset only gates the crossing (a rep whose crossing precedes the detected onset is flagged CROSSED_BEFORE_ONSET and kept as evidence). Onset therefore cannot move the crossing time, and the residual correlation is weak. The label does correlate with onset latency because both measure how quickly the player starts, not because the onset absorbs the gap.

question: Is the offset constant by player, game, alignment or speed?
key_statistic: between-player SD of mean gap / total SD, squared
note: the offset is a distance, so its time expression scales with 1/speed by construction; the per-player constant accounts for only the share shown. The plane offset itself is dominated by play-to-play movement (paired within_sd ~0.06 yd against a between-play SD ~0.23 yd), so a per-player calibration cannot recover it. See variance_decomposition.csv.
